data.long_meaning: Ilisha is a Sanskrit name derived from the term 'Ilani', which refers to the goddess of illusion and magic in Hindu mythology. This name is believed to be bestowed upon children born under the influence of the goddess, representing a life filled with creativity, mystery, and enchantment. The name Ilisha carries the meaning “Goddess of Illusion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ilisha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of illusion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

This reminds us of the power of storytelling and the important role it plays in our society, as well as the importance of believing in the power of the unseen and unimaginable. data.spiritual_symbolism: Ilisha, derived from the Sanskrit word "Ilasa," meaning "Goddess of Wishes Fulfilled." It symbolizes the divinity that grants heartfelt desires, inspiring hope and faith in the journey of life.

historical_references.reference: Ilisha was an ancient Hindu name for the goddess Shakti in Bengal, India. She was believed to be the guardian of the rice fields and the giver of prosperity. In the Bengali Puranas, Ilisha is mentioned as the wife of Shiva, who was known as Ishana in this region.

Another reference suggests that Ilisha was also the name of a queen of Kamarupa (Assam), a powerful medieval kingdom in Northeast India. She is said to have ruled during the 11th century and was known for her military prowess and patronage of art and culture.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Ilisha' is most commonly associated with the queen Hilsa fish, a highly prized ingredient in Bengali cuisine. This fish is considered a delicacy and is often cooked in various ways, such as ilish macher jhol or ilish paturi. The demand for Hilsa fish is increasing due to its unique flavor and high nutritional value. However, the population of Hilsa fish is dwindling due to overfishing and habitat destruction. As a result, there is a growing trend towards sustainable sourcing and consumption of Hilsa fish, with many restaurants and individuals advocating for the responsible harvesting and farming of this fish. This trend is reflected on various platforms such as Instagram, where many food bloggers and chefs share their ilish recipes and sustainable sourcing practices. On YouTube, there are numerous videos showcasing the different ways to prepare ilish and the importance of sustainable practices in the fishing industry. On Zomato, users can filter their search for restaurants based on their sustainable practices and can read reviews on the authenticity and sustainability of ilish dishes.
